headline: 雷托遭控 英倫文化速報
context: 演員兼音樂人傑瑞德·雷托（Jared Leto）被控性侵，BBC 調查報導指出，共有 10 名女性指控他有不當行為，包括與未成年少女發生性關係、傳送露骨訊息，雷托本人否認指控。英國文化圈同時還有幾則輕鬆消息：BBC Three 推出諷刺億萬富翁的模仿紀錄片，一篇個人隨筆談演唱會如何找回生活熱情，亞馬遜新片以鯊魚驚悚片登場，時尚專欄則聊起夏季穿搭的層次感。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: TikToker Shabaz Ali uses his uber-dry wit to make the mega-rich look ridiculous in this very silly satire BBC Three’s latest documentary opens with a man floating down a London street in a smart black turtleneck and grey suit jacket, increasingly alarmist string music swelling around him. “In a world of ever-widening economic divides,” he begins, gesticulating wildly to the camera as he walks through lavish Knightsbridge, “the BBC have asked me, Shabaz Ali, to answer one burning question: are billionaires bad?” You would be forgiven for thinking that this was another documentary of the kind the channel is known for: well-intentioned and well-made programmes, fronted by presenters such as Stacey Dooley and Zara McDermott. Then the camera zooms out to reveal another camera pointed in Ali’s face, and the music stops: “Er, yeah,” he says. “They are!” He strides off, mock end credits playing at triple speed. As it turns out, Shabaz Asks: Are Billionaires Bad? isn’t one of those BBC Three documentaries that boils down important societal goings-on for gen Z, but rather a parody of the genre. It’s a bit of a risk to send up one of the things your channel is best known for, as if ITV started broadcasting spoof versions of those dark psychological thrillers where a heavy-drinking police detective is haunted by an unsolved case from 20 years ago. sources.title: Shabaz Asks: Are Billionaires Bad? review – a hilarious spoof that’s like Philomena Cunk meets Louis Theroux

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: I was nearly 60 and hadn’t had sex in 10 years. And I was fine with that. But seeing the Verve’s former frontman reminded me how much fun it is to fancy someone When the world entered lockdown in 2020, I’d just moved into a new flat where, at the age of 56, I found myself living alone for the first time in my life. I’d been separated for nearly a decade from the father of my two kids – one of whom had already flown the nest. The other was just starting at uni. So it was just me and my cat, Trinity, in what I now thought of as my “forever home” for one. I’d embraced all those nice, selfish things about being single. I’d travelled alone, I ate when I wanted, went to bed when I felt like it, did housework only to please myself – and usually only in times of dire need. I reconnected with friends in a fresh way, as an individual. It felt empowering and less cluttered, after the years of motherhood and partnerdom. Mealtimes were at my own volition (well, and Trinity’s) and were a case of “Mmm, what shall I have?” rather than, “Oh God, what shall I do for tea?” I know people in decades-long relationships who would bite their own arm off for this level of autonomy. sources.title: A moment that changed me: I’d lost my libido – then I saw Richard Ashcroft on stage and it came bursting back

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: A group of holidaying friends get trapped in a cave system with a bull shark in a solidly entertaining B-movie lifted by a toxic central friendship We’ve officially reached maximum shark movie this year , with about six released so far and even more on the way and so the drop of yet another one, in the middle of Shark Week, raises a number of questions: is it in any way essential? Will anyone ever come close to matching what Steven Spielberg achieved with Jaws or, more realistically, Renny Harlin with Deep Blue Sea? How junky are the shark effects? And most importantly, at least for those of us watching the majority of them, is it more of the same or is there an attempt to do something even slightly new with the swim, stalk, slash formula? Trying something a little different is in itself extremely hit-and-miss because while I appreciated last year’s unusually striking Dangerous Animals for smartly inserting a serial killer into the mix, the addition of a hurricane to this year’s Netflix one-star dud Thrash meant that the film was both a terrible shark horror and a terrible disaster thriller. In recent months, we’ve seen Harlin return to the subgenre with Deep Water weaving in a plane crash and this week’s Antonio Banderas-starring Above & Below adding a drug cartel which makes the week’s other shark movie, Amazon’s gen Z-led offering The Devil’s Mouth, seem somewhat quaint in comparison. The special ingredient here is something a little less grandiose, but more potentially intriguing: a toxic friendship. It’s a movie that asks the rare question: what if you finally came to terms with how awful your best friend is just as a bull shark starts picking you off? Continue reading...
sources.title: The Devil’s Mouth review – Amazon’s shark thriller gives us just about enough to chew on

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Adding layers doesn’t have to leave you a hot mess – think sheer scarves and crochet with flashes of colour to elevate your look Perhaps I shouldn’t admit this, but I’m in two minds about summer dressing. Part of me believes summer is about joy, sunshine and good times, and clothes should embrace all of that. This woman loves Pucci and owns not one but two silver kaftans. The other part of me believes summer should be uncomplicated, laid-back and earthy. This woman never checks in luggage and has worn the same black beach cover-up for so many years it’s too threadbare to cover anything much. The thing is, either approach looks absurd if taken to extremes. Candy swirls, cherry prints and strawberry bag charms are delightful, but pile them too high and you look like a walking knickerbocker glory. And while white linen shirts and simple black sandals are chic, you risk looking a bit like you’re on a meditation retreat where the dress code is “wealthy disciple”. Know what I mean? 雷托遭控 英倫文化速報

演員兼音樂人傑瑞德·雷托（Jared Leto）遭 BBC 調查報導指控性侵，共有 10 名女性指出他有不當行為，其中包括與未成年少女發生性關係、傳送露骨訊息。雷托本人否認所有指控。同一時間，英國文化圈也有幾則輕鬆消息：BBC Three 推出諷刺億萬富翁的模仿紀錄片，一篇個人隨筆談演唱會如何找回生活熱情，亞馬遜新片端出鯊魚驚悚題材，時尚專欄則聊起夏季穿搭的層次感。

—— 本則整理自 BBC、The New York Times、The Guardian，2026 年 7 月 29 日發佈，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
threads_text:
英國文化圈今天訊息量不小，最重的一則是演員兼音樂人傑瑞德·雷托（Jared Leto）遭控性侵。BBC 的調查報導指出，共有 10 名女性指控他有不當行為，包括與未成年少女發生性關係、傳送露骨訊息，雷托本人否認所有指控。其餘幾則消息輕鬆不少：BBC Three 推出一部諷刺億萬富翁的模仿紀錄片，被形容像 Philomena Cunk 遇上 Louis Theroux；一篇個人隨筆寫到看完 Richard Ashcroft 的演唱會後，如何重新找回生活熱情；亞馬遜的新片《The Devil's Mouth》端出困在洞穴裡的鯊魚驚悚劇情；時尚專欄則聊起夏季穿搭如何靠薄紗和鉤織堆出層次感。

本則整理自 The Guardian、BBC 與 The New York Times 於 2026 年 7 月 29 日發佈的報導。
voice_text: 傑瑞德·雷托被控性侵，10 名女性指控他行為不當。這位演員兼音樂人的指控內容包括與未成年少女發生性關係、傳送露骨訊息，雷托本人否認所有指控。英國文化圈同一天還有幾則輕鬆一點的消息。有一部模仿紀錄片專門諷刺億萬富翁，手法相當戲謔。也有一篇隨筆，寫的是看完一場演唱會後重新找回生活熱情的心情。亞馬遜的新片講的是一群朋友被困在洞穴裡，還有一隻鯊魚在外面等。時尚版面則聊起夏天穿搭，靠薄紗和鉤織堆出層次感。
